_comment: Tier-2: skfem's ElementVector stores DoFs INTERLEAVED (x0,y0,x1,y1,...), not blocked (x0,...,xN,y0,...,yN). Naive `u.reshape(2, -1)` scrambles components across rows. The proper extraction is via `ib.nodal_dofs` (shape (n_components, n_nodes)) — `u[ib.nodal_dofs[0]]` is the x-component, `u[ib.nodal_dofs[1]]` the y-component. This is the canonical PR #20 pitfall verified operationally: the wrong reshape produces NON-matching values vs the correct nodal_dofs extraction. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 takes the second component split with the documented fix -- u[ib.nodal_dofs[0]] / u[ib.nodal_dofs[1]] instead of u.reshape(2, -1) -- so both paths agree. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 3 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'do not match' (the FIXTURE WARNING branch runs instead) so the fixture goes red. NOTE the other two expectations, 'ElementVector' and 'interleaved', are hardcoded prose in the header print and survive any mutation. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py FIXED 2026-08-08: dropped 'ElementVector' and 'interleaved', both in an unconditional header print. 'do not match' is gated on the measured np.allclose comparison and stays. The FIXTURE WARNING arm was caught by nothing -- forbid_in_output was EMPTY -- and is now forbidden.
